## Natural history notes

A medium-sized orbweaver characterized by a rounded abdomen with mottled reddish-brown, gray, or tan markings, banded legs, and reddish femurs that give the species its common name. In Florida, the Red-femured Spotted Orbweaver is found in gardens, yards, forest edges, hammocks, pine flatwoods, wetlands, and around buildings where it can anchor webs between vegetation or structures. It builds a circular orb web, usually at night, to capture moths, flies, beetles, mosquitoes, and other flying insects, often hiding during the day in nearby leaves, bark, or sheltered corners.
